analysis.title: G10 Inflation Monitor: Core Inflation Accelerates Outside Canada; Trimmed Measures Look More Benign
key_insights: Traditional exclusion-based core inflation accelerated year over year in September in Japan (2.4% vs 1.9% in August), the UK (2.8% vs 2.6%), the US (3.1% vs 3.0%) and the Euro area (2.5% vs 2.4%), and was unchanged in Canada (2.1%).

On a month-over-month annualized basis, exclusion-based core accelerated in Japan (6.0% vs 2.4%), the Euro area (3.6% vs 1.3%), the UK (4.0% vs 2.8%) and the US (3.9% vs 3.2%), but slowed in Canada (1.5% vs 3.1%).

US trimmed inflation runs well below exclusion core (Dallas Fed trimmed mean +2.3% yoy, GS trimmed core 2.1% yoy). GS US economists say trimmed mean remains a useful signal of underlying inflation because much of what is trimmed reflects one-off effects of tariffs, the energy shock, and AI-related price pressures and mismeasurement.
GS trimmed core slowed on a month-over-month annualized basis in Canada (1.3% vs 2.8%), the Euro area (1.8% vs 2.6%), Japan (2.2% vs 2.4%) and the UK (2.8% vs 3.4%).

GS harmonized core on a 3-month basis is generally close to central banks' preferred measures but is notably higher in Japan, where owned housing, which GS excludes from its harmonized measure, weighs on the official core.
September US core CPI surprised to the upside, driven partly by firmer owners' equivalent rent (+0.7% yoy as cited) and a large rise in toys and games (+4.2% yoy), a volatile category.

The BoC's preferred core measures both surprised to the downside in Canada, partly on sharp price declines in car rental (-3.9% mom) and travel services (-2.4% mom), which had run hot in prior months.

Over the last 12 months, monthly headline and core prints have both surprised to the downside outside the Euro area, with the largest cumulative core surprises in Canada (-80bp), Japan (-50bp) and the UK (-23bp).

On a 3-month annualized basis, core goods inflation accelerated in the US (PCE, 1.7% vs 1.0%, on autos and recreation goods), Canada (0.8% vs 0.4%) and Japan (5.7% vs 5.4%, partly 'naphtha-flation'), and edged down in the Euro area (2.5% vs 2.6%) and the UK (1.8% vs 1.9%). Part of the global core goods strength reflects consumer electronics price hikes tied to the surge in memory prices.

Core services inflation (3-month annualized) accelerated in most DMs, partly on firmer airfares: Euro area 3.1% (vs 2.0%), Japan 2.6% (vs 1.5%), US 3.3% (vs 2.5%), UK 4.5% (vs 3.8%); Canada ticked down to 3.5% (vs 4.6%).
Rent inflation (3-month annualized) ticked up in Canada (3.4% vs 2.7%) and the US (2.7% vs 2.3%), was flat in Japan (0.9%), and ticked down in the Euro area (2.4% vs 2.6%) and the UK (5.1% vs 5.2%).
Energy inflation (3-month annualized) accelerated across DMs: UK 52%, Euro area 46%, US 28%, Canada 26%, Japan -5% (price control measures resumed in September).
Food inflation accelerated in the Euro area (2.0% vs -0.1%) and the UK (1.7% vs 1.1%), and slowed in Japan (2.2% vs 5.4%), the US (-0.3% vs 0.8%) and Canada (-1.1% vs -0.5%).

Breadth: the share of the headline basket running above 4% (six-month annualized) moderated in Japan (37% vs 48%), the US (23% vs 24%) and the UK (48% vs 49%), ticked up in the Euro area (25% vs 23%), and is near historical average in Canada (21%). The share above 8% ticked up in most DMs except Japan.

GS forecasts Q4/Q4 core inflation to accelerate to 3.1% in the US (PCE, vs 3.0% now), 3.0% in the UK (vs 2.8%), 2.6% in the Euro area (vs 2.5%), 2.5% in Japan (vs 2.4%) and 2.1% in Canada (vs 1.9%), then moderate in 2027 to 2.2% US, 2.7% UK, 2.4% Euro area, 2.0% Canada and 0.6% Japan (food and beverage tax cut from April 2027).

GS raised 2026 Q4/Q4 headline forecasts by 0.4pp in Canada and 0.3pp in the US on higher oil prices and wider refined product margins. Euro area 2026 headline unchanged, 2027 headline cut by 0.4pp on faster fuel price normalization. Japan end-2027 headline and core (ex fresh food) nudged up 0.1pp on energy.
GS end-2027 inflation forecasts are generally below consensus (Exhibit 14).

risk_factors: Energy price pass-through: 3-month annualized energy inflation is 52% in the UK, 46% in the Euro area and 28% in the US, lifting the distribution of item-level inflation outside Canada.
Core goods pressure from consumer electronics price hikes tied to the surge in memory prices.
Distribution of three-month inflation rates across core items is skewed higher in most DMs outside Canada.
The share of the basket with rising year-over-year inflation ticked up across DMs.

tension_points.bull_case: GS trimmed core (2.1% yoy) and the Dallas Fed trimmed mean (2.3% yoy) run well below exclusion core (3.1%), because the gap reflects one-off effects of tariffs, the energy shock and AI-related price pressures and mismeasurement.
tension_points.bear_case: Exclusion-based core accelerated to 3.9% month over month annualized in September, core goods and services both picked up on a 3-month basis, and GS forecasts US core PCE at 3.1% Q4/Q4 in 2026.

theme_stances.key_argument: GS forecasts core inflation to accelerate in 2026 in most DMs before moderating in 2027 as upstream price pressures fade.
theme_stances.evidence: We expect inflation to moderate across DMs in 2027

theme_stances.key_argument: Trimmed mean inflation remains a useful signal of underlying inflation because the gap to core reflects one-off effects.
theme_stances.evidence: trimmed mean inflation remains a useful signal of underlying inflation
